content: SQLite concurrency for background-writer + concurrent-reader apps: default rollback journal mode = writer blocks ALL readers and vice versa; default busy_timeout=0 = immediate 'database is locked' on any contention. Required: PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL (readers and one writer coexist; persistent across connections; local-disk only, no network FS), busy_timeout=5000 on EVERY connection (per-connection setting), BEGIN IMMEDIATE for write transactions (deferred read-to-write upgrade fails immediately with SQLITE_BUSY that busy_timeout cannot fix). Long write transactions block all other writers for their entire duration - compute (embeddings) outside the transaction, commit fast. Checkpoint starvation: a permanently-active reader prevents WAL checkpointing, WAL grows indefinitely. VACUUM/DDL take exclusive locks. Sources: sqlite.org/wal.html section 9, tenthousandmeters.com 2025 SQLite concurrent writes, mako.ai transactions guide 2026, productionhardening.org busy timeout, zeroexp.dev locking model.
